title: The Promise of Junebug Creek
premise: Rafael Halloran inherited Junebug Creek Vineyard buried in debt and has spent seven years quietly rebuilding it while hiding the truth: he once ghosted his college love, Noa Reyes, after a catastrophic betrayal neither of them has named. When a snowstorm traps Rafael, Noa, and their mutual rival—wine critic Delphine Marsh—in the vineyard's crumbling farmhouse, seven years of silence thaw into confession, jealousy, and reluctant honesty. As Delphine's review could save or sink the vineyard, Rafael must choose between protecting his reputation and claiming the love he abandoned. He chooses truth over safety, confesses everything publicly at the harvest festival, and wins back both the vineyard and Noa.
about_author: Sebastian Oyelaran is a former sommelier who traded cellar work for storytelling, writing romances set in agricultural communities where land and memory run deep. He lives near a working vineyard he refuses to name, collecting weather reports and second chances.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Seven years after inheriting a bankrupt vineyard, Rafael walks the frost-bitten rows of Junebug Creek, tallying what little he has left. A letter arrives: famed critic Delphine Marsh will visit before harvest. The beat is weary hope—the sense that one visit could save everything.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Flashbacks interleave with Rafael preparing the guest house, revealing how he rebuilt the vineyard through caution and how a woman named Noa haunts every decision he doesn't make. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility.

chapters.title: Noa Comes Back Down the Mountain
chapters.summary: Noa's POV. Noa Reyes returns to town as the new co-op agronomist hired to consult on the valley's blight, telling herself Junebug Creek is just another client. She sees Rafael across the farmers market and her coffee goes cold. Beat: old grief disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: Professional Distance
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Their first meeting is all clipped professionalism—soil samples, pruning schedules—but every sentence carries seven years of unsaid things. Rafael offers her the consulting contract; she takes it out of pride, not forgiveness. Beat: tension under civility.

chapters.title: Delphine Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Critic Delphine Marsh shows up two weeks ahead of schedule, sharp-eyed and unimpressed, sniffing out that the vineyard's celebrated 'family legacy' is thinner than the brochure claims. Beat: the mask beginning to slip.

chapters.title: What Happened in the Twenties
chapters.summary: Noa's POV. Partial flashback: Noa and Rafael were inseparable until senior year, when Rafael vanished after an incident involving stolen research and a ruined scholarship—her scholarship. She never learned why he ran. Beat: righteous anger with a crack of doubt.

chapters.title: The Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. An early blizzard barrels toward the valley on the eve of Delphine's tasting. Roads close; Noa is stranded mid-consultation; Delphine refuses to leave without her tasting. Three people, one farmhouse, no exits. Beat: dread laced with inevitability.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Power fails; the three share wine, firelight, and forced proximity. Delphine, delighted by drama, pries at their history. Rafael and Noa orbit each other like magnets with opposite charges. Beat: warmth against hostility.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Rafael and Noa's shared POV. Late-night argument spills into a kiss that both immediately regret and don't. They agree it was a mistake—a lie they repeat while standing closer each time. Beat: surrender to old gravity.

chapters.title: Delphine Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. The critic watches the two of them circle each other and recognizes leverage—and something lonelier: envy of a love she's never had. She begins drafting a review that cuts deeper than wine. Beat: antagonist made human.

chapters.title: Confession in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Trapped in the barrel room during a blackout, Rafael finally tells Noa the truth: he took the blame for a professor's fraud to protect her future, then fled because staying meant watching her believe the worst. Beat: catharsis, but not absolution—she's furious he decided for her.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Choosing For Her
chapters.summary: Noa's POV. Noa rages—not at the sacrifice but at the silence, the way he erased her agency twice. She walks into the storm rather than stay. Beat: heartbreak as boundary-setting; love isn't enough if it comes with decisions made over her head.

chapters.title: The Review That Cuts
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Snowbound with wifi restored, Delphine publishes early: a devastating piece questioning Junebug Creek's authenticity and hinting at 'old scandals.' Distributors freeze orders. Beat: the career Rafael built begins collapsing.

chapters.title: Salvage Season
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The community rallies—Noa's co-op colleagues, the town that watched Rafael grow up—offering emergency contracts. But Noa stays away, and Rafael realizes the vineyard was never the thing he couldn't lose. Beat: found family holding him up while love holds out.

chapters.title: Delphine's Price
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Delphine offers a retraction and a glowing follow-up—if Rafael gives her exclusive access to 'the real story,' including the fraud and Noa's name. His reputation would be saved; hers would be reopened like a wound. Beat: temptation sharpened into a moral knife.

chapters.title: The Contract on the Table
chapters.summary: Noa's POV. Noa learns of Delphine's offer from a colleague and confronts Rafael—not to stop him, but to watch what he chooses. For the first time she refuses to guess, refuse to be protected. Beat: quiet, terrifying clarity.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Actually Costs
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael drafts the exposé, saves the vineyard on paper, and understands he'd be trading the only honest thing left. He burns the draft in the fireplace where they kissed. Beat: the choice made—not for her, but finally with himself whole.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival, Public Record
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. At the town's harvest festival, Rafael takes the stage and tells the whole story himself—the fraud, the sacrifice, the cowardice of his silence—before Delphine can sell it. The crowd's reaction splits; Noa stands at the back. Beat: climax; truth offered freely, outcome unknown.

chapters.title: Delphine's Second Draft
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Scooped and stung, Delphine rewrites her review anyway—this time honestly, moved by a man who chose ruin over a bought redemption. The new piece praises the wine and names the courage. Beat: rival becomes unlikely ally.

chapters.title: Orders Come In
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The honest review goes viral; orders flood in; the co-op offers a partnership. Rafael turns the first celebration toward the empty chair where Noa should be. Beat: triumph hollowed by absence.

chapters.title: Junebug Creek in Winter
chapters.summary: Noa's POV. Noa returns to the vineyard on the first snow, not to forgive but to renegotiate: partnership, honesty, and a rule that no one decides alone ever again. Rafael agrees to all of it and asks for nothing more. Beat: reconciliation built on terms, not erasure.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Shared POV, epilogue-style. One year later: the vineyard thrives under joint stewardship, Delphine's column opens with their story, and Rafael plants a new block of vines named for the creek. The promise of Junebug Creek was never about grapes—it was about staying. Beat: earned, warm resolution.
